cand.title: Interior Design Show Toronto 2027
cand.excerpt: Confirmed dates and venue establish the event; commercial accessibility and room demand remain to be verified.
cand.ledgerVenue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Verified organizer-side commercial entry points, not verified hotel-contract signatories: Catia Varricchio, Director, Sales & Strategic Partnerships, catia.varricchio@informa.com (also identified as Partnerships Director in the 2027 prospectus); Will Sorrell, National Director, IDS Canada, will.sorrell@informa.com. Catia handles partnerships/sponsorship inquiries; Will is the senior event-leadership escalation. Additional operational routing: Melanie Mora, Operations Coordinator, IDSOperations@Informa.com; Megan Mauracher, National Program Manager, megan.mauracher@informa.com. Ask these contacts to identify the actual housing/staff/speaker lodging buyer rather than assuming contract control.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced 28th edition: January 21–24, 2027, Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. These are activity dates, not publication dates, and fall within the requested horizon. The Getting Here body explicitly states opening and closing dates; the 2027 prospectus independently agrees. No official exact-date 2028 announcement was located; do not promote directory placeholders into confirmed future dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: a 157-room Harbourfront city hotel is suitable for selected exhibitor teams, international speakers/VIPs and small organizer groups, not exclusive accommodation or plenary hosting for the whole show. The brand site places the hotel near MTCC. A selective block in the supplied approximately 15–109 peak-room target range could be explored only after buyer and travel-demand confirmation; that is a sales sizing scenario, not published IDS demand. Side meetings are conditional on operational confirmation. The hotel brand explicitly says “Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice”; do not promise meals, hosted receptions or catering without separate written confirmation. This is a city-convention lodging fit, not a resort retreat.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 event venue is Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, 255 Front Street West, downtown Toronto proper, Ontario, Canada; not a hotel and not a resort. This establishes the announced event location, not visibility into the private venue contract or any accommodation contract.
findings.historicalRotation: Documented recent Toronto timeline: January 19–22, 2023 at MTCC South Building; January 18–21, 2024 at MTCC North Building; January 23–26, 2025 at MTCC North Building; January 22–25, 2026 at MTCC North Building; January 21–24, 2027 announced at MTCC North Building. This supports repeated Toronto editions and an intra-complex South-to-North change, not destination rotation. Vancouver is a separate edition, not evidence Toronto rotates to Vancouver.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown for Toronto 2027. No edition-specific official housing bureau, host hotel, named hotel block, booking cutoff, room allocation or open accommodation RFP was identified in the reviewed Toronto travel, exhibitor-kit and preliminary budgeting material. Consequently there are no verified Toronto 2027 block hotels to name; this does not prove no private blocks exist. The budgeting page says: “Other items to consider when budgeting for the show include staffing, freight/transportation, hotel requirements, booth design and booth build”. That signals an exhibitor expense, not an organizer accommodation commitment or proof of decentralized contracting. Its unauthorized-supplier section explicitly says listed companies including Convention Housing Service, EHS and Global Housing Services “are not affiliated with the show and do not have authorization to represent the show”; they must not be treated as housing partners. Vancouver hotel offers are not Toronto commitments.
findings.organizationStructure: Corporate exhibition organizer, not an association-owned convention: the official history states Informa purchased IDS in 2012 and describes Informa Canada managing Canadian shows. IDS is the event brand; Informa Canada is the organizer operation; MTCC is the venue. Hotels Canada co-creates the 2027 hospitality leadership program but is not thereby the show owner, housing buyer or appointed PCO. No external PCO/DMC or housing bureau was verified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No verified incumbent Toronto 2027 hotel or housing-bureau commitment was found; neither open sourcing nor committed-elsewhere status can be asserted. No sourced sellout, unmet overflow demand or room shortage was established. The 2027 prospectus reports 77% of its audience comes from the Greater Toronto Area, limiting the basis for converting headline visitors into hotel demand. MTCC already hosts the show and opening party; the exhibitor budgeting page directs show-day/party catering orders to MTCC. Radisson restaurant/lounge closure further limits a catered ancillary-event pitch.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Catia Varricchio first with a rooms-led, MTCC-adjacent subgroup proposal; ask her to route to the person buying 2027 staff, speaker and international-exhibitor accommodation. Ask who controls lodging, which hotels/bureau are contracted, whether supplemental blocks are permitted, and for actual peak rooms, stay pattern, rates, cutoff and attrition requirements. Copy or escalate to Will Sorrell if a strategic partnership decision is required; route logistics through Melanie Mora. Offer only hotel-confirmed available rooms and separately verified meeting services; do not quote a catered package while restaurant/lounge status is unresolved. If 2027 is closed, request the next Toronto edition sourcing timetable and an approved introduction path. Do not imply official-supplier status without authorization.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: January 2027 is confirmed, but commercial access to lodging is unconfirmed. Public named organizer contacts make a qualification approach feasible; no evidence establishes a live hotel procurement process, transferable inventory or authority to bypass any existing arrangements. Best conditional path is staff/speaker/exhibitor subgroup accommodation after organizer routing. The January 22, 2027 invitation-only Hotels Canada/IDS leadership roundtable is for up to 15 hotel industry leaders at MTCC; it is a potential relationship channel, not 15 guestrooms, an invitation for this hotel or an offsite venue opportunity.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated Toronto/MTCC editions support building an ongoing local accommodation relationship. If 2027 central lodging is already contracted, seek the next sourcing window, approved supplier criteria and introductions to traveling exhibitors rather than claiming current overflow. No official 2028 dates or hotel tender were located; future capture remains relationship development, not confirmed future inventory. Explore hospitality-program participation with the organizer only if appropriate; its published roundtable is already located at MTCC.
